sentence_stem: Yesterday I left my umbrella on the bus, so
correct_completion: I got completely wet on the way home.
full_sentence: Yesterday I left my umbrella on the bus, so I got completely wet on the way home.
acceptable_variants: I bought a cheap raincoat in the shop.
I walked home with my hood up.

options.text: I wrote a short message to my sister.
options.why_wrong: This is an unrelated action and does not show a result of leaving the umbrella on the bus.

options.text: I got completely wet on the way home.
I took the bus to the station early.
options.why_wrong: This describes a separate trip and does not complete the cause and effect started by 'so'.

options.text: I found the umbrella in my bag.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the stem, since the umbrella was left on the bus and it is not in the bag.

grammar_focus: Past simple with 'so' to show a result, using the irregular verb 'get' in its past form 'got'
explanation: After 'so', we need a clause that states the result of the first clause. Here the result of leaving the umbrella is getting wet, and the irregular past form 'got' shows the completed action.
translation: Wczoraj zostawiłem parasol w autobusie, więc w drodze do domu całkowicie przemokłem.
